meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'd like to know why my son has a zero.
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, and on what basis?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
People draft elsewhere and paste it in. Did you put this to Owen before the zero, or after?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Okay. I'm writing those times down. Is anything on his record right now?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
A misquoted line is a mistake, not proof of anything. Did you ask Owen where it came from?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Okay. You still haven't answered me: is anything on his record right now? Whatever happens here, it stays off his record and it stays quiet.
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay. That's called revising. What else do you have?

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Okay. To put this behind him, not because he did anything. In writing tonight, the zero off the gradebook, and nothing on his record.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
I'll confirm with Owen tonight. Put the day, the time and who supervises in the email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite under 4.4 on Thursday the twelfth after school, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on Owen's record. I still want the zero off the gradebook, an answer on whether anything is on his record right now, and the time and who supervises. I expect that in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Last position: she accepted a private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth, once she confirms with Owen, and she still wants it in writing with the zero removed, a clear answer on his record, and the time and supervisor; that is the fair outcome under 4.4, and her time did not run out first.
What moved her: You offered the private rewrite with nothing on his record and a written promise after your evidence had stood up to her objections, which met the demand she would never give up.
What cost ground: You left her question about whether anything is on his record unanswered for several turns, so she kept pressing it and read the silence as something being held back.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, with the text appearing late at night on October 28 just before the due date, came very close to that night, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked about his record, answer it on the spot, before moving on to the outline, so she has no reason to treat your silence as a dodge.
